optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Backend API Engineer, Equipment Maintenance Services
professionalSummary: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and the parts-availability service that queries depot stock for the technician app, including idempotency keys to prevent duplicate work orders. (src_abf2293d99c6)
Owned the integration test suite for both services, adding replay tests built from anonymised sync logs and keeping the suite passing in the CI pipeline. (src_d0cfe379b9aa)
Lined up each release with the app team and the platform team in the release review; deployments to production were run by the platform team's release engineer. (src_7443a7529d70)
Kept the API change log current, noting for each release that depot stock was refreshed only hourly, and maintained the on-call hand-over checklist. (src_67624cedce7b)
experienceHighlights: Two and a half years on the service-platform team: work-order and parts services, integration tests, release line-up and the change log. (src_97afd7c82f91)
projectsAndWorkSamples: Replay tests for the work-order API and one release's entry in the API change log; CI run numbers are included so they can be traced. (src_ee51234ba903)
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided materials establish the candidate’s development of the work-order API and parts-availability service, ownership of the integration test suite, coordination of releases with app and platform teams, and maintenance of the API change log and on-call hand-over checklist. They do not establish a documented, measurable reduction in work-order sync failures against a weekly baseline.
